newsitem.title: UK: Close Bros confident after H1 profits leap.
newsitem.headline: Close Bros confident after H1 profits leap.

text.p: UK investment bank Close Brothers Group Plc said on Monday a 30 percent increase in first half pre-tax profits reflected strong performances from all of its three main business areas, adding that its prospects were good.
"We remain confident of our prospects," the group said in a statement.
First half pre-tax profits rose to 28.2 million stg compared to 21.7 million stg for the same period the previous year.

Close Brothers said earnings per share were 15.31 pence, up 21 percent from 12.64 pence the previous year. The interim dividend was 3.8 pence per share, up from 3.2 pence the year before. It said asset finance accounted for 41 percent of operating profits, market making 33 percent and City merchant banking 26 percent. "As planned, the proportion of fees in our overall mix of income is increasing and during the period represented 25 percent," it said, adding this was up from 14 percent.

Close Brothers said the while bad debt levels were "slightly up", they "remain at historically low level". Competition on lending margins had been offset by "good discipline and fee related income". It said the asset finance side of the business, accounting for 71 percent of the group loan book, "continued its growth to new records in advances and profits" and the areas in which it specialises such as printing equipment, machine tools. light aircraft and used cars had all shown good volume growth. The group said the Hill Samuel corporate finance business which it acquired last year from Lloyds TSB Group Plc had been very successfully integrated "with no material loss of clients or staff'. It had led to "a quantum leap in the level of our activities and profits in this area", it added. Close Brothers said it continued to see organic growth in its activities. And while the forthcoming election in the UK might cause a temporary slow-down in some of its businesses, the UK economy remained strong and the group was confident of its prospects. -- Alexander Smith, London newsroom +44 171 542 7719
